source_ground_truth: At commit 37bc219ae4f5989d0bfaf6bfb917ae86108d33e1, main.main validates the ExecutionInput, initializes OrchestratorState, and calls run_codex inside the cycle loop. run_codex writes a temporary spec, builds the command, calls subprocess.run, and constructs an ExecutionResult from the returned process or caught timeout/FileNotFoundError. main validates the result, assigns last_execution, appends it to history, calls route_decision, validates the decision, and stores last_route before applying it. Routing checks success, blocking DSL state, stuck-loop status, then error-specific branches. Main applies retry or repair counters when the selected route allows continuation. The source does not provide a concrete input or subprocess outcome, so it cannot determine one actual final route. Because history is appended before routing and _detect_stuck_loop appends the current error again, two consecutive same-type failures can fill its three-entry check.

run_codex serializes the DSL and selected validator/metadata fields, builds a configured or default command, and calls subprocess.run with workspace cwd, captured text output, and a timeout.

Completed exits map to SUCCESS or FAILED; nonzero output is classified in ordered text-pattern checks, while timeout and FileNotFoundError have separate failed-result branches, and the temporary spec cleanup is attempted in finally.
main validates the result, records last_execution and history before routing, validates the decision, and stores last_route.
For failures, route selection gives blocking DSL state precedence over stuck-loop detection and error-specific branches; the listed per-error route choices match the source.
Applying retry or repair updates the stated counters when eligible, and the repair hook is not implemented; main passes the same ExecutionInput on subsequent loop iterations.
Appending the result before routing lets two consecutive same-type errors produce three matching entries in the stuck-loop check; test-result heuristics do not themselves determine the route.
